value_raw: Instruction Générale des Opérations de Change (IGOC) 2026, effective Jan 1 2026 — the most significant reform to Morocco's capital-controls regime in years; resident foreign investors holding investments 10+ years can transfer up to MAD 2M/year (~€185,000) abroad without original proof-of-financing documents; individual travel/transfer allowances raised across the board
notes: Primary source: the Office des Changes (Morocco's own foreign-exchange regulatory authority) — its own publication announcing IGOC 2026, corroborated by Lawyard, AMERELLER, MoroccoWorldNews, NorthAfricaPost. Sits on top of the 2022 Investment Charter, still in active rollout. No tightening, expropriation threat, or foreign-ownership rule reversal found anywhere — the confirmed direction of travel for foreign capital specifically is opening, not closing

fact_label: Restricted-nationality list (e-Visa required instead of 90-day visa-free entry)

notes: Benin, Brunei, Cambodia, Guatemala, India, Israel, Jordan, Laos, Thailand, and Vietnam are routed onto Morocco's e-Visa track (30 days, one 30-day extension, 60 days total) instead of the standard 90-day visa-free tier (one 90-day extension, 180 days total) most Western passports get. Source list explicitly non-exhaustive ('among others') per moroccan-visa.com/e-visamorocco.com/Wikipedia's Visa policy of Morocco (cross-corroborated 2026-07-08) - treat these 10 codes as a confirmed floor, not a confirmed-complete set. A narrower carve-out exists for Israeli citizens born in Morocco (visa on arrival with Moroccan national ID) or holding a Council of Jewish Communities of Morocco letter (evis.ma) - not reflected in this row, which states the general-population rule.
